utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, I wanted to ask you about Exhibit 1788, and do you have that on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this a page from your database?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can -- I would like just, as a general matter, to go through and have you explain to us what you put in your database. And if we can just go through a page -- I mean we can see it ourself, but can you explain how you created the database.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The first thing we tried to nail down was the building name. And we tried to include alternative forms of name so that anyone who looks at it, if they encounter it by the other name, could at least link it to this particular data field. Then we included the municipality or district, the names of the town in Serbian and Albanian. We had a GPS device with us. And sites we visited personally, we always took a GPS reading in order to -- well, for two purposes: One is to enable us to map our results once we got back; and secondly, to make it duplicatable so anyone could go to the same site and see if that is indeed where we were. Then we included the dates of construction and reconstruction, if possible, what historical site. Then we included in information on the official status. The former Yugoslavia, like many countries, had antiquities legislation, under which certain buildings were declared to be listed monuments. A listed monument under this Yugoslav legislation meant that it was under legal protection. It could not be altered or demolished without permission, and certain amount of state funds were made available for restoration. Then we have some categories of the building use and building type, which are useful in the database for generating statistics, among other things. The building setting - this was an urban setting - the most important one is of course the building condition --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll down on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: So we have a simple visual description of what we saw. And you can see that we saw scattered piles of rubble, the stone foundations. We were able to identify some of these, such as parts of the minaret and the ablution fountain. We saw evidence of how it happened. There was a large, knocked-down utility pole, which was also visible next to the mosque in the pre-destruction photo. And it was completely charred on one side, so presumably that had been exposed to fire. And then some remarks about the context, which you can also see in the bottom photo here; namely, that the more than buildings surrounding the site were intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see, at the bottom, there is a listing for surveyor.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How did you decide whose name went in there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Basically, who was holding the camera; the other person would be taking the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see the top photo, on this page, is by someone named Xhavit Lokaj. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Xhavit Lokaj is a member of the staff of the Institute for The Protection of Monuments of Kosovo. And in the summer of 1999, after the end of the war, he took a lot of photographs. And he was willing to share them with us. We liked to get his photographs because they were taken in the immediate aftermath of war, whereas we were there four months later. So sometimes they show sites before they had been tidied up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in your database are these photographs in colour?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have a couple more photos, pre-war, and these are from a gentleman you met before, Raif Virmica.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Virmica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go down to see the informant's statements at the top of this screen. Now, can you explain how you put this information, where you get it from, and how it's entered.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Basically when we were visiting some of these sites, there would be people who would be gathered to watch us take pictures and some of them would come forward and say they saw what happened. If what they said sounded like it would be potentially of interest, we took down the basic information and took down their names and contact information accessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where did you record that information, as far as contact information?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: We had survey sheets that we carried with us, and for each site we filled it in, along with the damage description and the GPS reading. We would also put in information such as this. And then once we got back in Cambridge and we developed and scanned our photos, we then keyed it into the database.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So the contact information for the informants is in the database.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where in the database? Is that a separate section?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No, it's usually at the bottom. In this case Mr. Mejzini was at a loss because he was about to leave town and was not able to give us a new address. I assumed, since the family is well known and it's a small town, anybody truly interested from your Pristina office could have gone and run him to ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is there any more information on this page at the bottom or is that it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. And so you see at the left Mr. Mulaku, the town archivist, who is also mentioned in that Financial Times article that was referred to earlier --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: -- he was one of the people who showed up when we did our survey in Vucitrn, and so we have the phone number for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then lastly in your database you have a bibliography and media accounts, if any, about the particular site.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Anything else to comment on that page?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to Exhibit P1807.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second, Mr. Hannis, until I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- check something. Is Vucitrn a murder scene? Is it part of paragraph 75?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Paragraph (i).

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: (i), yes, 72(i). It relates to a convoy. And you'll recall, this convoy was not -- was actually on the road between Vucitrn and elsewhere, not in the town itself. It's in the municipality but not in the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's on the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the media account related to the various mosques we've been looking at. It also includes reference to murders on the 22nd of May. Now, that's not part of the indictment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, it's not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Ivetic, you'll see that this Financial Times report does include material which can be compared with the information given by the informants on the previous page, but also includes additional material which goes out with the indictment. Now, our approach will be to exclude from consideration material that doesn't fall within the ambit of the indictment. But to take account of media reports which quote people and can be compared with other information given by the same people, that seems to us relevant; what weight we give it is quite another matter. If that gives you some guidance on how this document might be used, then it may enable you to focus any other objections you take. I qualify this, of course, by saying that because of the nature of these indictments you can never be absolutely sure that a subtle prosecutor isn't going to be able to point to a sentence construed a particular way as including something that's in this document. But we will view this document as essentially a document relating to cultural heritage and to the issue of persecution that's raised in Count 5 and not as a document which goes to the other elements, unless the Prosecution, before completing this witness, indicates parts of this report that they claim are relevant to other counts in the indictment. Now, is that of use to you in deciding what needs to be objected to here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, and I've talked to my colleagues during the break and what we intend to do is, rather than object through each and every single excerpt and take up more time, we'd rather, at the end of the Prosecution's direct of this witness, give a summation of all the specific objections that we have with respect to specific excerpts so they can be dealt with at that time rather than doing the same argumentation 10, 15 times throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We would find that helpful. Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I need to indicate for the record that I misspoke earlier when you asked me if Vucitrn was a murder site. I said, "Yes, it was," and I referred to 72(i). I meant 75 (i). Thank you. All right. Now, if we could look at Exhibit P1807.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have that photo on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Riedlmayer, what is this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a picture that we took of the mosque in the centre of Suva Reka, a town north of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And my brightness and contrast on the photograph on the screen isn't all that good. Can you indicate to me what is the damage to this mosque.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you look at the right-hand corner, first of all, you see something that should be there and isn't. Mosques, in general, in this region of the Balkans, have the minaret at the right-hand side of the entrance, and the minaret here is missing. Where the minaret should be, there is some damage to one of the small domes and also to the corner of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this a photograph of the same building?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is the same building. I've just gone around the right-hand corner and taken this photo of the stump of the minaret. You can see at the bottom of the photo the base of the minaret, and to the left of that is the beginning of the arcade, at the entrance of the mosque. What you can see, by looking at it, is that the structure has ballooned outwards, developing these vertical fissures, because clearly there had been a blast inside the minaret itself. Minarets are hollow and have a staircase inside so that the man who gives the prayer call can climb up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can go to Exhibit P1779 next, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is this an entrance from your database concerning those photographs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is an entry for that mosque. It's Xhamija Bardhe, which is Albanian for white mosque. It gives the street address. The mosque was built in 1520, but then in 1990, all but the minaret was torn down and replaced with a new mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll down to the bottom half.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. At the very bottom you see a photo taken just before the war by Mr. Virmica. You can see the minaret in place. It's a picture taken from behind the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I note in the information, it's indicated that the minaret was a remaining historic part of the mosque. Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Meaning that it was a 16th century mosque. It had been in very bad repair. And in 1990, when they re-built the main prayer hall, they left the historic minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the source of -- well, let's go to the next page and if you can tell us the source of your information about how this damage came to be done.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, if you scroll down. We encountered a local man who lived across the street from the mosque, just 200 metres down the street, and he described the time when it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The contact information is at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll to the bottom of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you personally speak with this individual and record this information?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go now to exhibit -- well, is there one more page, I'm sorry, one more page in this exhibit. And the bottom half regarding the media account.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you have these media accounts in hand before you went to sites or did you collect them after you had been to a site? How did you come to put them in the database?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, again, thanks to working at a large university, I have access to LexisNexis, and I did extensive searches of the news databases and collected these accounts, both before and after, in the process of compiling the database.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we move on to the next one which relates to Celine village in Orahovac, I want to first ask you, did you testify in the Milosevic trial about a mosque being destroyed in Celine or damaged in Celine?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you aware that Mr. Milosevic argued and presented witnesses to indicate that there had never been a mosque in Celine village?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which witness or witnesses testified to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I don't have the exact names of his witnesses. I believe there was a former low-ranking army officer who had been on the scene and there -- anyway, I remember reading news accounts where he boasted that there had never been any.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you do some research after that to gather any additional information about the existence or non-existence of a mosque in Celine before 1999?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, since I had pictures of the destroyed mosque but had not had a pre-destruction photo, I decided to make a good-faith effort to turn one up, if possible, to see whether, in fact, there was anything to the allegation that there had never been a mosque in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we show the witness Exhibit P2445, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a picture of the mosque in Celine taken on the eve of the war. I obtained it through the good offices of the secretary of the Islamic community of Kosovo, who, on my behalf, went to Orahovac, which is the nearest town to Celine, and asked the secretary, the local Islamic community, whether such a photo could be found. And he turned up a photo of the mosque as well as an official copy of the entry in the cadastral register concerning the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what the cadastral registry is.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The cadastral registry is the land records office. It was maintained before the war by the Yugoslav government, and since June of 1999, it's been maintained by UNMIK, the UN Mission in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May we show the witness Exhibit 2444. And, Your Honour, I should indicate, for the record, on our list of exhibits we intended to show this witness, we have the ERN numbers mixed between the cadastral register record and the photograph. The photograph is ERN 06046518 and the cadastral register is 6519.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is this the document you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what does it indicate about a mosque in Celine?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you scroll down, sir, you will see that it has, first of all, right above that the ledger from which this is an extract. Then it has the name of the owner indicated as "The Islamic Community of Kosovo, Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Local Council of the Islamic Community of Orahovac." And then below it it has entries for the building, which is 56 square metres, and the surrounding plot, which is 466 square metres. Although no date is indicated for the building, by appearance, it's a modern mosque, and the fact that the owner is referred to as being in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, it means that the mosque clearly existed before 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And under "Place Name," can you translate for me or explain what's written there.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If you go up a bit, it's at -- near the top of the page. It says here "Municipality Orahovac," is the Serbian name; Rahovec is the Albanian name. And then "Cadastral Zone," Celine is the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how do we know what type of building it is, that it is a mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: If you scroll down, you can see it. "Xhamija," X-h-a-m-i-j-a, it means mosque. It's under "Place Name."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit P1800.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the photo of the destroyed mosque in Celine. I would draw Your Honours' attention to the structure in the middle there, the curved structure. It is layers of concrete into which have been inset bricks, the ends of which show at the edges. And if you go back two pictures, you can see in the before-picture the same structure around the balcony of the minaret. The bricks are a very distinctive, decorative element added to the bottom of the muezzins balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you use the pen to draw a circle around the structure you're describing.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, can we give that an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And my apologies, could we return to Exhibit 2445.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that structure that you drew a picture of from the damaged photo, to what do you believe it pertains on the pre-war photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is this decorative detail at the bottom of the railing of the muezzins balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we give that an IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC90, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the damage you saw to this mosque would be described as what, heavily damaged or completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, next, if we could have P1773 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This will be another page from your database pertaining to this particular mosque, and anything --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the bottom half of the page? Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It indicates the source of the photograph. It came from Mr. Sabri Bajgora at the Islamic community of Kosovo. I also included the information from there. And if you scroll down the way down, you can see that the information came from two separate sources; one came from the Islamic community, accompanied by that photograph, and the ruined mosque also is included in the IMG database that was compiled in early 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what information was included in the IMG database?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The IMG database also had a very similar photo of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could we go to the next page regarding the source of your information regarding the destruction of this mosque.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: There is no next page on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So the information about the destruction was based, in part, on your own viewing.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit P1806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on, what we have is a statement, "Mosque burned down and ruins bulldozed by Serbs ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "According to Islamic --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: "... according to Islamic community." Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Meaning when I obtained the photograph from the Islamic community, it came with this information. I don't know what more I can say. I wasn't there when it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, something you could tell us further, in your view, the statement that it was burned down and then bulldozed is that consistent with what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, certainly it looks like a leveled building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Can you comment on whether it was burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you go back to the original photograph, you will see two things: First of all, you see some charred timbers sticking out; secondly, you see that the rubble is collapsed in a heap. If the mosque had been blown up, you would have expected the rubble to fly outwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The difficulty with that, of course, is that it's been bulldozed by the time you see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly. So it's very hard to tell very much from a pile of rubble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anyway, that's one that you haven't sought to verify in any other way, by going back to the community for more information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You haven't done that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, basically I went back for the additional information about the pre-war existence of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which also then produced the pre-war photo which shows the structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But as far as what happened to it, no, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And as far as who did it is concerned, really - and this is no criticism of you at all - you're not providing any reliable information about who did it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm simply passing on the information that was given to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would be directing the Court's attention to other evidence that's been presented in this case in connection with those matters. Next, if we could look at Exhibit P1806.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, can you tell us what this is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photograph that I took showing the 16th century mosque of Kel Hasan Aga - that's K-e-l, H-a-s-a-n, A-g-a - in the village of Rogovo, which is north of Prizren. What you see is the stump of the blown-up minaret. You can see the initial steps of the internal staircase which has been clearly blown up with explosives placed within. You can see that both from the way that the rubble is lying and also from the main structure itself, which has radiating cracks and part of the dome has been knocked away by falling rubble. To the left is the forecourt of the mosque which has also been smashed by falling rubble.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what classification is this damage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This was heavily damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit 1784, P1784.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this had an official status?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. It was a listed monument. It had been published in the scientific literature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Under "Building Setting," on the right, I see a "set relationship." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is a technical term in architecture, whether or not a building adds positively to its setting or whether it's eyesore. "Negative discordance" means that it sticks out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And "positive discordance?"

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Meaning that it's an asset to its setting. It's a harmonious building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who made that classification?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That was something Mr. Herscher insisted on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: You may recall that the database was meant to serve, not only for the Tribunal, but also for planning purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Planning what?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Meaning for restoration, conservation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does positive discordance refer to its status when it was in its pre-war condition?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the bottom half of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And these are photos you and Herscher took?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. The after photos, yes; the before photo came from Mr. Virmica, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. In the original version, you would actually see the mosque. It doesn't reproduce well in black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to 1784 -- I'm sorry, that is 1784. If we could go to the next page of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the source --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: To the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The source of your information?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Basically, we talked to the man who owned the store across the street, and he had information on somebody who allegedly saw this. We passed that on again, in the expectation that if it was of interest, this would be a way of tracking down the eye-witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to Exhibit P1792.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a different mosque you're moving to or is this the same one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Pardon me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you moving to a different example?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because I want to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The -- each of these documents has the name of the surveyor. In this particular case, it's Mr. Herscher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Others have reference to the EU/IMG database.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's also reference to Sabri Bajgora.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the case where the surveyor is identified in that way, did you also see the building in its damaged state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unless -- unless, at the bottom, either Mr. Herscher's name or mine is mentioned, it is not one of the 144 sites we visited in person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Next exhibit, P1792, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's on our screen now?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is a photo of a mosque in Bela Crkva, which is another village near Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you describe the nature of the damage that's depicted here.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Again, what you're looking at is the entrance is to the left, and the brown stump, with the big hole above it, is the remains of the minaret. You can also see, if you look carefully, that the top of the dome has been scarred by falling rubble. I assume the minaret had been blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what did you base that on?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, again, if you look carefully at this photo - and also subsequently, I assume, you will show the database entry and other photos as well - you can see the remains of the minaret. You can see the hole in the building, and the signs of falling rubble.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go to the database entry P1774. And this one was classified as heavily damaged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Given that it had multiple damage to the roof and to the interior and to the external wall, it was multiply compromised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: To the bottom half of the page, please, all the way to the bottom, if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is not one that you personally visited?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's not one that we personally visited, but we had information from multiple sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And photographs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I probably should remember this, but who is Sabri Bajgora?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sabri Bajgora was the deputy mufti of Kosovo; the second in the hierarchy of the Islamic community of Kosovo. And he had an personal interest in what happened to Islamic houses of worship houses in the war. So right after the end of the war, the end of summer in 1999, he travelled around Kosovo, took pictures, and collected pictures. And when we arrived in Kosovo, one of the places we visited was the Islamic community. And he offered to make his photographs available, and, initially, he wanted to just give us a CD. But when we said that the original photographs would be preferable, he gave us the original photographs. We returned with a suitcase full of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is he actually referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he's mentioned as one of the sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was he a source for a number of your pre-war photographs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Some, but most of the photographs were post-war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Down to the bottom half.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: There's nothing at the bottom half.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. No information other than from the database of the IMG and from --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And a photo taken right after the end of the war from CNN. That one I just took off the CNN web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then is there a third page here that has the media --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the third page and the related media accounts. Let's move next, then, to Exhibit 18 -- P1801, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do that, again I'm thinking ahead at the moment, but one of your media reports there --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would that be The Scotsman, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, at the top of the second column, refers to "NATO satellite photos showing ... before and after." Now, are these on your database or do these then have to be accessed by going to the web site which is referred to in the newspaper article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. The satellite photos are on a web site, unfortunately. I assume they can be downloaded if they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you look at these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I did look at them, and, you know, among other things, it is a photo of the mosque showing a tall minaret, so it can't be claimed that the mosque never had one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Indeed, in that regard, was Bela Crkva also a place that Mr. Milosevic and his witness indicated there had been no mosque existing prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Defence counsel should turn all microphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does this fit in as a piece of evidence in the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The satellite photos, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, or is it not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see the satellite photos and/or hear from a witness from Bela Crkva talking about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, so they'll come later --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- or have we seen them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- I think we have seen them, but I have to double-check. I have something in mind that I think these relate to, but I have to consult the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go, then, to Exhibit 1801, P1801.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a picture of the mosque at Cirez; that's C-i-r-e-z in Serbian and Q-i-r-e-z in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the nature of the damage seen here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I would -- I would say that it is almost destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In other words, the building is not salvageable, but you still see some identifiable elements of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit P1778.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your database pages reference this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The typical entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the bottom half of the page and all the way to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is another one that you didn't see yourself.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did not see it myself, but I had a pre-war and post-war photo from Mr. Bajgora, and it also showed up with photos from the EU/IMG database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the heading "Damage," who is responsible for that comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That, again, came with the photos from Mr. Bajgora. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not your assessment of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And can you say whether that's consistent with what the photographs demonstrate, or is it just impossible for you to make a conclusion on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it's very hard to tell from the photograph whether this was done by impacts or projectiles or somebody detonating something inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we've got to get that information from another source.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, a couple for which we don't have photographs here. P1786, I think, is a page from your database. Can you tell us what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is an old mosque in a village called Kotlina, in southern Kosovo, in Kacanik. If you scroll down, please, you will see that I saw the photo of it in the EU/IMG database. For technical reasons, Your Honour, we were unable to extract the photos from the IMG database, but we did submit it along with the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. My understanding, yes, you introduced your report and your database in the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And at that time you included a disk you had received from IMG concerning their database.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But at that time neither the Registry nor the Court nor the Prosecution were able to open that particular disk.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Oh, really?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My question is: Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you brought a new disk of that database?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I can send you one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But you have seen the photo that pertains to that --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it matches the damage you have describe here.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it's lightly damaged, and it is vandalism inside.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Meaning it looks smashed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can go, then, to Exhibit P1787.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us about this one.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is another village in the south, near Kacanik. It's a mosque in a village called Ivaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you have a photo for this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I do, courtesy of Mr. Bajgora again. It's not a site I visited. In the database, once again, it's in colour and much clearer, but what you're looking at is the gutted interior. The roof is missing. The interior is charred. And what you're looking at, although it's hard to tell from this, is the mihrab wall, which is the wall facing Mecca with the prayer niche.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the informant information about this one indicated that the damage occurred before the NATO bombing started.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, and that is not only from Mr. Bajgora, but in this case it's corroborated by a first-person report from Reuters which had a correspondent in the village in early March of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can we go to the third page of this exhibit for that media report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is that the one you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, please show Exhibit P1793.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just hold on while I observe this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The indications in this report, Mr. Riedlmayer, are that there may have been a KLA cell in the village in question. Now, you told us earlier about damage that might be consistent with the firing of projectiles in the course of conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the building being caught up in that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, there are two sources of damage referred to here. There's projectile damage as well as fire damage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what would we make of such evidence, as there is, about projectile damage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the projectile damage, all I can tell you about is that there are signs of it on the photo. You can see some impacts. Clearly, the damage to the mosque was in two stages. The news report doesn't mention that at the time the reporter was there it had been burned out yet, and so clearly, from the photographs, at some point subsequent to that it was burnt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the newspaper report is important in identifying the stages in which damage may have occurred here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Although, the statement on the first page is completely burned out -- "shot up at close range, and burned by Serb forces March 10, 1999" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- which is not entirely accurate now that we look at the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you know, I don't know at what point subsequent to the reporter's visit the fire may have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I have just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, that's one we would ask you to read in conjunction with the other evidence. We have had a witness testify, Mr. Loku, about Ivaja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I think I was asking for Exhibit P1793. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you see that photo on your screen, Mr. Riedlmayer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's that a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That's a mosque in the village of Brestovac; it's also in Orahovac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's the nature of this damage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you can see the minaret has been decapitated. You can also see that the mosque no longer has a roof. You can also see marks of fire. And on a better photo - I have the original print - you can see through the door into the interior, which is a huge pile of rubble. The exterior walls are also badly cracked and the timbers are burned. So I think the building is essentially unsalvageable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit P1775 in your database entry. How would this be classified.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I classify it as "almost destroyed," meaning an unsalvageable building but with identifiable elements still standing above ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you have a pre-war photograph of this mosque?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I did not. I don't think there's any arguing that it wasn't a mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The source of the information about the date and the cause of the damage?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's, again, Mr. Bajgora and the IMG database.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go now to Exhibit P1794.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe we're still in Orahovac municipality.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: We are, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is this, and where is this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a picture of the mosque at Velika Krusa, or Krusha e Madhe in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And any opinion about the nature of how this damage occurred, and what's missing?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: To the left you see the entrance, and to the right you can see the remains of the minaret. And, once again, there are signs that this was caused by a massive explosion. Among other things, you can see the cracks in the exterior wall and damage to the roof and to the dome from falling masonry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's move to Exhibit P1776.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this one described as heavily damaged because?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Because there was extensive damage to the interior, for which I also had photos, and to the roof and to the external wall. It was not merely a question of the minaret being amputated; the building itself was compromised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom half of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the bottom photo is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The bottom is a view of the interior. Again, in the database in colour, you can see details that are not immediately evident from the black and white copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page regarding media reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, again, this is not one site that you visited personally?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No. It's not a site I visited personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next Exhibit P1802, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, as far as the cause of this damage is concerned, is there also other evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The cause of the damage, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. You've got an informant here, which is a human rights group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But has there been a witness on this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On this mosque, I believe we have had testimony. And I'm checking for a minute to get that reference. But as to the -- was your question as to the nature of how the damaged was caused?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. My question is to the informant's statement; the bit that's highlighted, which is presumably the bit that you consider to be the most relevant, actually attributes the damage to Serb soldiers with benzine, the mosque. Now, the source of that is an Albanian human rights group.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I ask the witness a question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, my question to you, first of all, was whether there are other witnesses dealing with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe we had a witness talking about the mosque in Velika Krusa, but I'm checking the record to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, as far as this informant's statement, there's a portion here that's bolded. Do you know who put that portion in bold lettering?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did. Simply because it's the only part that refers to the mosque directly. If you scroll further down, you can also see a media account from the German Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, which has a description of the damage as of June 19th. So that gives you a date antequam before the damage happened. It's the next page down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't, on the face of it, attribute the damage to anyone in particular, though, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have any further information on that at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go then to Exhibit P1802.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what that is? Where it is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It is a mosque in Mitrovica, in the north of Kosovo. It's the Ibar mosque. It's the one next to the famous bridge, across the Ibar river, which figures in this report as the scene of repeated conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This, I believe, was one of our photos from Mr. Virmica, taken in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we then go to Exhibit P -- Well, I'm sorry, is there a second page for this? Yes. Could we go to the second page for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what's that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That is the site of the Ibar mosque, in the summer of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess you would classify that one as completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you were able to determine that this is the site of the mosque that was in the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Because, in addition to the previous photograph, I also had other pre-war photographs - one of which is included in the database page you're about to play - and because I had a pre-war site plan that was published in the 1980s, showing its location immediately next to the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And is the bridge in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The bridge is to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go then to Exhibit P1780. And scroll to the bottom half, please. And all the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you saw this one yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Actually, I visited Mitrovica, in March of 2001, and saw the site. The site is pretty much as shown on the photograph from the summer of 1999; not much changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's media accounts at the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, okay. One more page then. I'm sorry. All right. Now, if we could go --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The suggestion here is that there may have been bomb damage. Do you rule that out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's hard to tell much of anything from a bulldozed site, so I draw no conclusions. I merely presented whatever information I could find. The suggestion here comes from Mr. Oliver Ivanovic, who is a Serb leader from northern Mitrovica. He claims one thing. The other media accounts simply describe what happened. The residents in -- according to one account, that the mosque had been looted, burned, and bulldozed. So I don't know. I mean, all I can tell you is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you went in 2001, although that was some time after the destruction reportedly occurred, did you see any surrounding damage that would be consistent or inconsistent with bombing from above?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No. The buildings across the street were fine, and certainly the bridge right next to it had not been hit by anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The suggestion is that the police headquarters were the target for the bombing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police headquarters are at some distance down the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And were they struck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were struck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How far away were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say more than a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, Exhibit P1798, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us about this picture.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is an interior photo of the mosque at Vlastica, which is in south-eastern Kosovo, and there's not a lot to say about it. There's clearly been an intense fire. You can see that even the window-frame has been charred and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move, then, to your database page, P1785. Do you recall -- did you see this one yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is not a village we visited ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And is this the only photograph you had of this site?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, this is one of the instances where this is the only photograph we had. But I was able to examine other photographs of which they did not -- were not able to give me copies, so I have a somewhat broader view of the building, which is where I concluded that it was heavily damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was the nature of that additional damage that led you to evaluate it as heavily damaged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there was damage to the roof. The fire extended all the way into the minaret, and basically all the combustible elements in the building had been destroyed. And while it was a modern building, it will probably have to be knocked down before it can be re-built.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the bottom half of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the source for this information was the IMG database and Mr. Bajgora?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The other photographs you're referring to came from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this was at the offices of the Islamic community, Mr. Bajgora again. But there were some photographs he was able to give us copies; others, not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the third page of this for the media account.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's all the information you have concerning that site?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, it's from a very long on-site report from Washington Post reporter David Finkel published in late 1999, and he just mentions having passed by the burned-out mosque. But not a lot of detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, Exhibit P1803, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a site I personally visited. It's the mosque in Landovica, which is right next to the highway heading north out of Prizren towards Djakovica. And what you're looking at is the -- really looking from the verge of the highway, a piece of the minaret which has tumbled down. You will see additional pictures on the database entry which show great holes in the dome and more pieces of the minaret lying on top of the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's move, then, to Exhibit P1777.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How did you describe the damage of this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Again, we called this heavily damaged, mainly because the main dome itself had been so heavily impacted that it was in danger of collapse.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can we scroll down to the bottom half of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us something about those two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll up slightly to show both photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here you see the hole in the cracks of the dome and the pieces of the minaret lying on top of the roof and an interior view looking out at the dome, with a great gap in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to Exhibit P1795.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's shown here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the library of Hadum Sulejman Efendi, an Islamic endowment library, a waqf library, in Djakovica town, north of Prizren. What you're looking at is the rear of the building. The little niches in the walls were where the books used to be. You can see evidence of fire, charred wood, and soot marks on the interior. And at some points subsequent to the burning, the minaret of the adjacent mosque, which you can see the dark spot on the right of the photo, was decapitated by a projectile and fell on the back of the building, collapsing the rear half of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before we move on, I think you described this as an endowment library or some other kind of library. I didn't catch that word.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's an Islamic endowment library. The technical word is "waqf," w-a-q-f. As a pious deed, people give money for educational and cultural purposes and establish these endowments. This library was originally established in the 16th century by an endowment -- by a local gentleman named Hadum Sulejman Efendi, and then the library itself, the building, was re-built in the 18th century. It housed the very important collection of manuscripts and rare books, as well as the archives of the Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were those books damaged in the process?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: They were a complete loss.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit P1783.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this one, then.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Classified as heavily damaged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Heavily damaged. In fact, it was eventually decided that it couldn't be restored and was knocked down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you see this one yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: I did. I actually went into the ruins to look to see what had actually collapsed. I was wondering exactly how it happened, and I found identifiable remnants of the top of the minaret that had smashed the rear of the building. I found pieces of the minaret's balcony that were easily identifiable, so I could tell why the rear of the building had collapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we go to the next page of this indict -- of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So at the left is a photo I took of the charred front and the entrance of the library.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And below you can find more information. I interviewed a gentleman called Xhahit Boshi [phoen], who lives in Gjakova, who claims to have seen it, so he was there. And I also had an interview with Professor Nehad Krasniqi, who was the keeper of rare books and manuscripts at the national and university library in Pristina and who was familiar with the contents of the library. So he gave me a statement about what was in the library before it was burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, please, Exhibit P17 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where would this fit into the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is described in -- if I can get this reference. In paragraph 72(h)(i), "On March 24th, 1999, the old mosque in the historic quarter, which included the bazaar, the Hadum mosque and the adjoining library, were among several cultural sites substantially or totally destroyed." This is in the deportation paragraph, 72, but we would argue that the destruction of these are part of the systematic campaign of terror to drive the Kosovo Albanians out. So even though it's not listed specifically in paragraph 77 as a religious site or a mosque that's destroyed, it's part of the historic quarter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, and about halfway down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. So -- and yet the destruction wasn't until May, it would appear --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of the mosque, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The destruction was at the end of March, when it was presumably burned. It wasn't until May that the top of the minaret was shot off and fell on the back of it. By that time, I assume, it was a gutted building due to the fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The mosque was actually attached to the library, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it on the next picture, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the damage, in May, was exclusively to the mosque, rather than to the library, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the damage in May was to the minaret. The mosque was also set on fire in March --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. But did the falling of the minaret damage the library in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what sheered off the back of the building, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't have a clear picture of this, Mr. Hannis, but it's probably me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not necessarily, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So, initially, in March your information is that the library and the mosque were both set on fire?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. If you move on to the next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: -- it may become clear, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit P1796, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What are we seeing here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Just to orient you, what you're looking at is part of the Hadum mosque complex. So it consisted of the mosque, which is the dome building that you see with the arcade at the centre rear of the picture. Right next to it is the front of the library which is still standing. The other photo you saw was from the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So where in this photograph is the library?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Just to the right of the mosque. You can see it. It has a little finial on top of the tower roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You're pointing to the upper right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Right. Then at the left, the big pile of rubble was an Islamic Koran readers school, which also housed the offices of the local Islamic community, which faced the mosque and the library. And according to, certainly, the evidence of intense fire that I saw, the destruction at ground level was from fire. Then between the mosque and the library stood the minaret. It was structurally attached to the mosque and towered over both the mosque and the minaret. In the database, I have pre-war photos that may make it clearer. And the top of the minaret, just below the balcony, had been sheered off. And in the minaret, below the balcony, there were a series of impact holes, approximately a foot across. So, clearly, someone had been taking pock shots at the minaret, until the top came off. When the top did come off, it hit the back of the library building and sheered it off. And, according to informants, that happened two months after the initial fire. So I don't know if that makes the sequence a little clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this photograph, the minaret is already knocked down?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, the minaret wasn't entirely knocked down, just about the top third of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if it were still standing, where would you see it in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: You would be seeing it, essentially -- you see the bottom of it. It's in between the library and the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Oh, all right. I do -- just to the right of the pillar that goes all the way up in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the fire in the library, is that what damages the books and the contents of the library?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In March?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: In March.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the fire in the mosque occurred at the same time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. I think I understand better now, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Could any books be salvaged; manuscripts or books --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: -- which you would have seen in a burned shape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was completely burned out and filled with rubble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have any photographs of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, the photograph you just showed was of the rubble-filled interior of the library.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hannis, is that a suitable time to interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again, we'll have to break, Mr. Riedlmayer. So if you could go with the usher. We'll see you in about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we will resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we next have Exhibit P1782.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this will be the database entry referring to the mosque. And was this -- this was one of the protected buildings in Kosovo; yes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's one of the more significant buildings in Kosovo, yes. It was under legal protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you had some additional photographs of this, other than the one that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we scroll down to the bottom half.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we'll have you tell us about those.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The one on top you can see the layout a little more clearly. The mosque is at the left; the building with the pyramid-shaped tile roof on the right is the library. And you see there the decapitated minaret.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: And below is another close-up of the charred portico.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And the source of this information about when and how this came to be damaged.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: The source of the information came from a number of sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, it's not listed here on the informants' statements, unfortunately. I don't know how that happened. But anyway, first of all, it was widely reported in the news that the mosque had been damaged on that particular day. And we also talked to the local Islamic community, who confirmed what happened. Most of what we did was constate the actual damage. I don't think the date of damage of the actual mosque itself is in dispute. What seems to be in some dispute, according to what happened in cross-examination in the Milosevic case, is the cause of the damage. Now, according to informants we did speak to, and I'm sorry that the statement doesn't seem to be in this copy, the sequence was that on the first night of the NATO bombing, after the Yugoslav army base in town was hit by missiles, about an hour or two later, groups of Serb military and civilians apparently converged on the bazaar and started setting fire to the mosque and to the shops. This is what the local Islamic community and various other people told us at the time. According to accounts in the Belgrade press, and according to the White Book issued by the Yugoslav government, they claim that the mosque was hit by NATO bombs. We did not see any signs of blast damage; what we did see was extensive signs of fire damage. The main damage to masonry was the toppling of the minaret, and on the minaret itself, we could see the impact of projectiles at various levels and then the top sheered off and landed on the back of the -- of the mosque library. On the picture you see on the screen right now, on the right is a pre-war photo which shows the minaret complete. It also shows the extended portico. The original portico had been extended in the 18th and 19th century to cover most of the courtyard to allow for overflow congregations, and that structure was built of wood. So when the mosque was set fire to, all of that burned. And over the entrance of the mosque, above the massive wooden doors, there was a semicircular lunette, an opening, which, according to the imam of the mosque we talked to, had been a source of complaint among the elderly congregants who complained that in cold weather a draft came in and so they'd covered it with a piece of wood. Apparently that's what saved the interior of the mosque from being burned. According, again, to the imam we talked to, the piece of wood had been struck by an incendiary projectile they tried to fire into the mosque. We could see the burnt piece of wood - and I have photographs of it - but the main prayer hall was not affected; however, the entire extended front area had been burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You used the word "lunette" to describe that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
