utterances.text: Yes, it's just a semicircular opening above the main door.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How do you spell that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: L-u-n-e-t-t-e; it's a French word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, Xhahit Boshi, whom you referred to earlier, is he the imam you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let's see. Yes, he is one of the people we talked to at the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In your last statement, you say, "according to the imam of the mosque we talked to ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe he is the imam we talked to, but I would have to consult my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You say that both the Belgrade press and the White Book that you have referred to claimed bomb damage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At what date did they claim that the bombing had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first night of the bombing, which would have been the night of the 24th/25th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not the May date when the damage was done to the minaret.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The May date is subsequent. And, again, local people told us that the top of the minaret was taken down in early May by ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say "local people," are you referring, again, to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Islamic community of Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go to the next page of this exhibit regarding the media accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, again, there was a reference to a satellite photo on a web site. Did you get a chance to look at that photograph regarding the bazaar being burned?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. And that one, I believe, was submitted in evidence in the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Following the allegation that the NATO bombing had destroyed the mosque and the historic centre of Gjakova around it, NATO released the satellite photo showing the burning of the bazaar in progress. And it's a quite detailed satellite photograph. I don't know if you have it available, but it shows the mosque still standing, a plume of smoke coming up from the library, and on the street immediately adjacent to the mosque, for a distance of several city blocks, all the shops have had their roofs burned off. And so you see little empty niches, you know, for several hundred metres' length. And to either side, the densely built-up urban neighbourhood, there's no sign of any kind of scattered damage which you would expect in any kind of aerial bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we next go to Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have this photograph, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a photograph which is the one I think he's talking about, but I won't know until we come to it in the chronology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Exhibit P1797.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us what this shows.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This shows this street immediately adjacent to the mosque where you have these long rows of bazaar shops with the dividing walls perfectly intact but interiors completely burned out. Again, you would expect that if there had been aerial bombing there would be blast effects and these rather insubstantial brick walls dividing the buildings would have been affected. I believe you also have a pre-war shot which shows you what these buildings were like. The entire medieval bazaar district was a protected area. Under legislation, it was a historic site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we go to the next page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a photograph taken in January of 1999, so just two months previously, of the bazaar, same street. You can see there buildings with tile roofs and brick dividing walls and then the structure itself made of timber and plaster.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where would the mosque be in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It would be off to the right and behind the shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Exhibit 17 -- P1781.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, here you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: So this is the entry for the old market surrounding the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we've seen the pre-war photograph at the top. The photograph at the bottom of that page, have we seen that one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, the photograph at the bottom - again, you would see it much better in the original colour - shows flames shooting out through the shops. It was, allegedly, taken by a local Djakovica resident, while the market was being burned. It was distributed by international news agencies in June of 1999, and that's how I got a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And here you have, at the left, is a photo showing residents, who have just come back after the war, trying to clear out salvageable items from the burned-out shops. And at the right is a view from the mosque - actually taken from the minaret of the mosque. You can see the shadow of the photographer - of the street adjacent to the mosque with the bazaar shops. That appeared in a book on heritage of the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. At the left you have another informant statement from Mr. Xhahit Boshi. And he claimed that on the first night of the NATO bombing, he heard, on the radio, that the centre of Pristina and Djakovica had been bombed by NATO. Since he was a resident of Djakovica himself, he was wondering what was going on. And then at some time later, he heard cars coming and the beginning of the burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to Exhibit P1789.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, this is your report, but included within this exhibit are some photographs, I think the first ten pages. So I'd like to show you and ask you to discuss those, if you could. They may not be in your hardcopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But if we could have the first page of Exhibit 1789 on the screen. Yes. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm told there's a technical problem, but is that 0 -- K0218764?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's Exhibit D000-0747, which is listed as being 89 pages in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. But the first page that you're after, what's the particular number of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a photograph. I have a hardcopy; perhaps we can put it on the ELMO and have the witness describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, Mr. Riedlmayer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What's this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: It's a photograph I took inside the mosque, in a village called Crnojevo, or Caralleve [phoen] in Albanian. It's on road heading south, from Prizren towards Brizrem, just where the road enters the mountains. And the mosque had had some projectile impacts, and the minaret had been damaged. So we went to check it out. We went inside and found the interior vandalized, partially burned. And the entire floor of the mosque was covered, not only with rubble and rubbish, but with torn up Islamic books and scriptures. There were many empty book covers, whose interior had been torn out, and some of the pages had been defecated on. You see here part of it. I have other photographs showing it. I collected all the pieces of paper that I could. And, out of an interest, later on in the evening, I tried to sort it out and found the remains of more than 20 different books and manuscripts; all religious books, which had been ripped to shreds and then defaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And let me show you next, skipping one page in the sequence, to K0218751.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Oh, it would be page 3 then of the e-court version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We may have it now on your screen.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the remains of a Serbian Orthodox monastery church in Dolac. Dolac is in Klina municipality in northern Kosovo, north-western Kosovo. And we were investigating reports that it had been blown up, after the war, by returning Albanians; and we found this. It was an old church with a tile roof, and clearly an explosive had been placed inside, blowing out the walls. And the heavy slate roof - I'm sorry, not tile roof - had literally crushed what remained of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next photograph, please, next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is very near to the previous picture. It's a village called Drsnik, that's D-r-s-n-i-k. It is also in the municipality of Klina. And we went to visit it, because in the Yugoslav government White Book, it was claimed as one of the Orthodox churches which had allegedly been hit by NATO bombs. We found that the church, in fact, had an intact roof and an intact door. But someone had gone inside and set fires and, subsequently, had scrawled the letters UCK, U-C-K, which is KLA in Albanian, over the door. And inside we found more graffiti and damage from the small fire that had been set inside. But it's clearly not damage that had been done from the air. And since, according to media reports, first-hand media reports, the village had been continuously occupied by its Serb inhabitants until the middle of June 1999, it is unlikely that this happened until after they left; namely, in the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, can we go to page 9 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is a photo of.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken in the Kosovo capital of Pristina by a Reuters photographer, Oleg Popov. I purchased this from the writer's news agency. The photograph shows the historical archive of the Islamic community. Burning in the background is the Emperor's mosque in Pristina. It was taken, I believe, on the 15th of June, just six hours before the arrival of the first British KFOR troops in Pristina. According to news accounts which were simultaneous to the taking of this picture, the burning was done by a group of Serbian police who rushed into the building, and then after they emerged the building burst into flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In connection with your report, did you prepare some maps to graphically show the locations of the damaged sites that you visited and took information about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe it's at e-court page 28 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is the first one I'd like you to explain for us. And, I'm sorry, this is black and white, but I have colour copy that we could hand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think I have enough to give one to the Bench and one to the Defence -- oh, I'm sorry, I only have two. Perhaps we can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, could you explain to us what's depicted here.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: What we are looking at is the map showing all the damaged sites that we either visited or documented in Kosovo. The different colours refer to the different types of damage -- I'm sorry, the different monuments of different categories. What you have at the bottom, the coloured dots indicate -- in the case of the yellow dots, are civil monuments, meaning non-religious monuments, historic architecture; the red dots indicate Islamic sites; the blue dots are Catholic monuments; and the purple dots are Serbian Orthodox monuments. The size of the dot indicates the number of monuments damaged in a given municipality, so some places, such as Pec in north-western Kosovo, Djakovica, or Vucitrn, have larger dots than some of the villages where only one or two buildings were documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to page 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have another hard copy for you. It's another map in your report. What's this intended to show?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is a mapping of the Serbian Orthodox monuments that were damaged in the period between June and October of 1999, after the end of the conflict. We have no mapping of anything that happened before that because we have found no convincing evidence that any Orthodox monuments were damaged before the end of the war. Again, you can see there are clusters of them in various places, and in some places the dots are larger, indicating multiple monuments that were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next page, page 30 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have one more hard copy for you. I think this relates to the Islamic sites.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This represents the Islamic religious architecture that was either destroyed or damaged, and again you see large dots in places like Djakovica or Pec and smaller dots spread throughout. Would you like me to comment more on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the first thing you can see is that the damage isn't localised; it extends throughout much of Kosovo. The areas where you don't see any dots indicate areas, for example, here, in the south, which has a predominantly ethnic Serb population; but, very interestingly, also, this southern-most tip of Kosovo, the Goran region, which is almost a hundred per cent Muslim but the Muslims living there are not Albanians, they are Slavic Muslims, the Gorans, and they had generally good relations with the Belgrade government. Similarly, in the area between Prizren, Djakovica, and Suva Reka here, virtually every village mosque that we were aware of had been damaged or destroyed, with one single exception. There is a village called Mamusha, M-a-m-u-s-h-a, just north of Prizren which is predominantly ethnic Turkish and there the mosque was intact. The villages surrounding it were ethnic Albanian and the mosques had been burned down in every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, I would like to show you Exhibit 1808. Did you prepare a chart to show the relationship between the damages to the religious sites of the three different ethnic communities or religious communities?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think this is in colour in e-court and should be on your screen shortly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you explain this for us.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Basically, the colours represent the various communities. Red is the Catholic community; yellow is Orthodox; and blue is Islamic buildings. And what you see here is a series showing the degree of damage. Obviously, the largest number of buildings are those which suffered relatively light damage, and to the right is increasing degrees of damage or destruction. What strikes one about the chart, in general, though, is the disproportionately large number of Islamic monuments that have suffered destruction or damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see the yellow block for Serb Orthodox, that there are, what, 13 buildings that were totally destroyed and seven almost destroyed.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have information about when that damage occurred?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes. Both from our own survey and from information received from the Serbian Orthodox church, this destruction happened almost entirely in the summer of 1999, between the end of the war in mid-June and our arrival there in October. We did not include any damage subsequent to October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I have just a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could we, Mr. Hannis, take in-court pictures of pages 28, 29, and 30 of Exhibit 1789, since the electronic version's not in colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe we can get colour versions into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Of these three, rather than just take pictures of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We can do either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We could substitute colour versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm told the best way is, in fact, if you put them on e-court, but it would be helpful to have these colour versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I may have a moment to consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There is one other exhibit I wanted to address with you, Mr. Riedlmayer. It's Exhibit P1550, 1-5-5-0. These are some additional entries from your database, but I think they pertain to -- other than Islamic monuments, Serbian Orthodox and Roman Catholic. If you could tell us a little bit about each of these.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the complex of the patriarchate at Pec. It's the seat of the Serbian Orthodox patriarchate and one of the most important buildings in Kosovo as far as Orthodox religious heritage is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how was it you came to investigate this site?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: There had been allegations in the Yugoslav government White Book that the monastery had been damaged by NATO bombing, and we visited the site. Also, a conservator, Tody Cezar, who is an expert in mural paintings, did an investigation of the interiors. Furthermore, the Italian government's institute for restoration, the Institute di Rettorato, sent an expert team in 2000/2001 to examine the monument and none of them found any sign of damage, other than from rising damp and long-deferred maintenance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of this exhibit, and the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's simply your bibliography concerning that site.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us, this is Gracanica.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on. Did you, Mr. Riedlmayer, see the patriarchate in Pec?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this one? Tell us.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Gracanica, there were also allegations that it had been damaged during the NATO bombing campaign. We visited the Gracanica and once again Today Cezar, the paintings conservator, was engaged by UNMIK's Department of Culture to examine the murals and found no visible sign of any damage either the murals or to the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we scroll to the bottom all the way on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was what you saw consistent with the photograph here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And no evidence of severe damage from NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go three more pages to the next new entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And these are pre-war photos of that building?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page, please. Bibliography. Next page, please. And scroll to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us what this one is.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is a close-up of part of the Kosovo battle-field memorial. It was built in the 1950s under Tito and was also the site of the famous 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo. It was also a place we visited because there had been allegations that it had been directly hit by the NATO bombing, and we found, in fact, that there had been no damage that we could see, other than to -- unfortunately, again, the black and white photo doesn't do it justice. But surrounding the actual memorial there were these cut-off concrete tubes which contained flood-lights, and the concrete tombs -- tubes had been decorated with cast-iron decorations with a Serbian cross and the two dates of 1389 and 1989. And somebody had clearly gone around and pried these off. You could still see the dirt shadows of where the cast-iron had been attached to the concrete. But other than that, there was no visible damage on the outside. We were not allowed inside the monument, which has a stairwell and a look-out on top. But the guards stationed at the door said that somebody had set off an explosive inside the stair-well which had damaged the stairs. But there was absolutely no sign anywhere at the memorial or next to it of any damage from air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And that's --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: That, again, is a poorly reproduced photo of the memorial itself which I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next page. Sorry. Okay. And to the next page. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about this one, Mr. Riedlmayer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is our entry for the Franciscan Priory Church of St. Anthony in Djakovica. It's one of the more notable examples of Roman Catholic religious architecture in Kosovo. It was built near the end of the Ottoman period, in the 19th century. And, again, we visited it because there had allegations that it had been hit by the NATO bombing. The church itself was very close, only a couple hundred metres from a Yugoslav army base which had, in fact, been hit by the air-strike. We could see the damaged barracks and other buildings. But the church itself was in perfectly good condition; no damage done to it. Adjacent to the church was the convent and the rectory, and there we spoke to the parish priest who had been present when all these events happened. He said that half an hour before the NATO air-strike actually occurred, he and the nuns had been evicted from the building by the Yugoslav military, who then took up residence both in the convent and in the church while the air-strike was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was there damage to the windows from the bombing of the nearby --

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Well, the windows of the rectory, he said, had been blown out by the air blast, and we could see when we visited in October of 1999 that the windows had been recently replaced. He also said that computers and other equipment and furniture within the rectory had been looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go three pages on to the next item in this exhibit. No, I'm sorry, the next page and the next one after, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The media accounts concerning the one you just told us about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now could we go to the next page in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about this one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is in Pec, which is north of Djakovica and where you had a very similar arrangement of the city quarry. You had the city's main mosque surrounded by a bazaar district. And according to the Yugoslav government's White Book, both the main mosque, known as the Barakli [phoen] Xhamija, or the mosque of Mohamed the Conqueror, and the surrounding bazaar had been hit by NATO air-strikes. As far as the mosque was concerned, the damage we saw was inconsistent with any aerial attack. The dome, the roof, the interior had -- the dome and the roof were in good condition and the interior had been burned out. The surrounding bazaar had very similar kind of damage to that which was seen in Djakovica. If you could scroll down you could maybe see from --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you scroll to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, it's poorly reproduced, but you should have the colour photos in your system. We have a pre-war photo taken just a couple months, before the war, at the end of 1998; and in the same street thereafter. What was remarkable about this, once again, is that over a distance of several city blocks, all the shops fronting the street had been destroyed and the rubble bulldozed into the back of the site. The whole row of buildings, following behind, were completely intact, as were buildings across the street. Again, this is not the kind of damage you would expect from an aerial bomb; that bomb is that precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page I note, under the surveyor column, there is a blank, but is this one you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is one I saw there myself . And, I'm sorry, I must have neglected to put that in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who would have been the surveyor for this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go -- skip the next two pages and come to the third page for the next site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, can you tell us about this one.

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: This is the one we earlier saw a colour photo of; this is the church at Dolac. You can note that it was a listed monument, meaning it was under legal protection as cultural heritage of exceptional value. And it was very badly destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is the one with the slate roof tiles, you told us about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Exactly. And you can tell from the GPS coordinates that this is site that we inspected personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, with regard to your database, is there a particular type of software that needs to be used to open it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRAS JANOS RIEDLMAYER
utterances.text: Yes, it's known as File Maker.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I don't have any more questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, just a moment. Mr. Riedlmayer, or maybe Mr. Hannis, one of you, where is the evidence of the -- what you've been describing as "the false allegations of damage by bombing?" You've described the White Book containing these allegations. Do we know if that's an exhibit in the case? Where do we find these, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have it presently. I don't know if it's currently on our list or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well is it part of your database, Mr. Riedlmayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not part of the database. I assumed that a copy was in the Tribunal's library. It's not limited to cultural heritage. It's a two-volume publication. If necessary, I can certainly provide photocopies of the relevant pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we don't want to be shadow boxing, so there's obviously got to be a target for these claims in the evidence. Now, Mr. Hannis, I still am not entirely clear about the Exhibit 1789. Largely, but not exclusively, the material, which appears in your 65 ter summary, is a repetition of these various extracts which you've been referring to. There's a great deal of duplication in the presentation of this material, I think. And, indeed, we saw that also in relation to the photographs. When we were looking at Vucitrn, we have, according to the list P1799, an enlarged photo of the shell of the Vucitrn municipality mosque. And you then had other -- another exhibit dealing with the actual damage, similar to what's on the screen at the moment. But we also discovered in the photographs, photographs of damage to two other mosques in Vucitrn, for which we don't, at the moment, I think in the course of the evidence, have the similar documentation to what we see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Your Honour. That photo series included five photos of three different mosques. And the Exhibit P1788 is only the extract from his survey about the old mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can ask the witness if, in his database, there is information concerning the other two mosques from Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The database has entries for both of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm not sure, because I have to double-check and see, if that may be a couple of the unaccounted for ones in Exhibit P1789, if you follow me. There are a couple of ERN ranges that were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. But I think that the Prosecution job here is to identify the parts of the report that are relevant to the indictment, and it may be you've actually done that in the course of this presentation, but you left hanging this suggestion that the database would also be an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we had tried to do that because of what we saw as the Court's view about us presenting extraneous evidence to specific items in the indictment, and so rather than trying to present the whole database regarding 548 sites, we tried to select those that are the ones specifically mentioned. But initially, we had everything under his report because I wanted to present them one at a time, and then we pulled out and had separate exhibits that resulted in some duplication. But unless the Court wanted the entire database, we didn't think that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there's been the odd comment by Mr. Riedlmayer, such as, "There's a colour photograph somewhere." Whether he was suggesting a print or something on his database wasn't clear to me, but he was suggesting --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The latter, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- some other material not identical to what's here but a better example.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think he's saying that yes, that's correct, that there are colour photos in his database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Riedlmayer, when you said that, were you referring to the database or were you referring to a separate print in colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have both, but the database has all the colour photos. And so if you are having software trouble, I do have a self-executing version of the database on a disk which I can provide you with tonight or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, now that you've started your testimony, I don't think it's appropriate for me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I don't know the answer to that, Mr. Hannis. If you do have a problem, then you've been told that something can be provided. And I don't think anybody's going to be concerned about the witness assisting in that way. It's possibly better if he does it after he's completed his evidence, but it won't be a problem for him to do that. But finally, would you tell me how it is you think that the database would assist us beyond the parts of the report that you've extracted and presented in the course of this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, only as -- in the sense that it's the entire document, and I think, in time, when you look at a report and only look at a portion of it, you may not be getting an accurate picture. But maybe in this context what we have presented is all you need for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think our position is that if there is other material in the database, it's for you to identify it and draw it to the Trial Chamber's attention, rather than for us to go fishing through such a large mass of material without the parties knowing what exactly it is we are using it for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Riedlmayer, about one thing in your report. When you were talking about your various sources - and they're identified in section A2 of the report itself - you referred to the IMG database, for example, and you're quite critical of its reliability in some respects. How have you used that in the course of your preparation of the report? Did you confine it to photographs or did you actually make use of other information as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We essentially confined it to using the photographs. The reason I'm critical of it is, as I explained, it was put together by local teams in various municipalities, some of whom had -- seemed to have different standards as to what to include and how to describe it. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is their database part of your database?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's a separate one. For technical reasons, I could not just snag the photographs out of their database and implant them into mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The KBI that you referred to, the Islamic community of Kosovo, has their database or all that material been incorporated into your database?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They gave me actual physical prints which I scanned and put into my database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it the same with the Serbian Orthodox eparhe [phoen] of Raska Prizren?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the Roman Catholic diocese as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what about the Institute for the Protection of Monuments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On page 21 you refer to a Mrs. Saha Rasam [phoen], a Canadian architect, who was a consultant for UNMIK and she had carried out a comprehensive survey of all kullas. There's 44, it says, that had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And of these 44 -- I think you refer to 45 as being part of your summary. Those 44 are not identical to the 44 of the 45 that you looked at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, thank you. That completes the first stage of your evidence. Tomorrow there will be cross-examination. You need to be back here in time to re-commence at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, I'll formally tell you, although I'm sure you're well aware of this, that you must not have any discussion about your evidence meanwhile; that you keep yourself to yourself so far is the evidence is concerned. You can talk about whatever you like with whomsoever you like as long as it's not the evidence in this case. If you can now leave the courtroom, we'll see you again at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 31st day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
